# Every `--json` payload is a machine interface, so its keys must be
# snake_case. Go serializes untagged fields under their Go name, which makes
# a stray PascalCase key an easy accident - the regex below catches any key
# (a quoted string followed by a colon) that carries an upper case letter.
#
# TestJSONOutputIsSnakeCase in cli/commands guards the same rule at type
# level; this script checks what the commands actually print.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

exec sesam add secret.txt --group dev
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev

exec sesam ls --json
stdout '"revealed_path"'
stdout '"access_groups"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

exec sesam user list --json
stdout '"sign_pub_key"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

exec sesam id --json
stdout '"name"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

exec sesam status --json
stdout '"revealed_path"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

exec sesam verify --json
stdout '"success"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

exec sesam log --json
stdout '"changed_by"'
stdout '"seq_id"'
stdout '"previous_hash"'
! stdout '"[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z_]*":'

-- secret.txt --
s3cr3t
